full_judgment: 3. The only question for adjudication in this case is whether the seizure of the trawler took place within the territorial waters of Bangladesh. Admittedly Customs Waters extends to the whole of Bangladesh and it includes the. Bangladesh Customs Waters as defined in clause (P) of section 2 of the Customs Act which provides that Bangladesh Customs Waters means the waters extending into the sea to the distance of 12 nautical miles measured from the appropriate base line on the coasts of Bangladesh. From item 8 of the seizure report. Annexure 'B' in the petition, it appears that fishing trawler was seized about 16 miles west of Cox's Bazar which has been taken to be an area well within the territorial waters of Bangladesh. According to the definition of Bangladesh Territorial Waters in the Customs Act as mentioned hereinbefore, it must be within 12 nautical miles measured from the appropriate baselines on the coasts of Bangladesh. The seizure report and the affidavit filed by the Government do not specify as to, whether this 16 miles west of Cox's Bazar is inclusive of the area covered by the baselines on the coasts of Bangladesh. The seizure report of the Customs authority and the affidavit filed by the Government on that account suffers from clear ambiguity and vagueness and on that account the benefit of doubt must be given to the petitioners concerned when on the face of the seizure report and the affidavit of the Government it clearly appears that the fishing trawler was at 16 miles west of Cox's Bazar. Thus, on the face of this statement it creates a presumption that the seizure took place outside the territorial waters, of Bangladesh. There is no material on record to show apart from this vague statement made by the Customs authority and the Government that the seizure actually took place within the territorial waters of Bangladesh as defined in clause (P) of section 2 of the Customs Act. That being so it must be said that the customs act had no jurisdiction to seize the trawler and the fish at about 16 miles west of Cox's Bazar since customs law evidently does not extend to such area.
